observations.statement: A standard CDCL solver that terminates after polynomially many conflicts and emits a Resolution trace yields a polynomial-size Resolution refutation on every unsatisfiable input.
observations.support: Expand each first-UIP conflict analysis into at most polynomially many Resolution inferences; see proof_attempts/H048/REFUTATION.md.

observations.statement: Explicit general-Resolution lower bounds are policy independent: the same hard family forces superpolynomial conflicts for every fixed standard CDCL branching, restart, and deletion policy whose proof log remains Resolution.
observations.support: Combine O038 with the explicit expander-Tseitin Resolution lower bound; see proof_attempts/H054/RESOLUTION_TRANSFER.md.

observations.statement: Every erroneous SAT circuit has a short local certificate once one erroneous formula is known: a witnessed false negative, a terminal false positive, or a violation of Shannon self-reduction on one restriction triple.
observations.support: Follow a false-positive branch through canonical restrictions until a local inconsistency or a fully assigned false terminal is reached; see proof_attempts/SAT_SELF_REDUCTION.md.

observations.statement: Proof-preserving preprocessing cannot evade a lower bound on the target proof system when the preprocessing log and the final proof compose with polynomial overhead.
observations.support: A short proof of the preprocessed formula plus a polynomial Resolution derivation of the preprocessing steps would give a short proof of the original formula.

observations.statement: From H060 onward, a new hypothesis must name its parent hypotheses and state a material delta; a renamed or merely weakened restatement is not an admissible descendant.
observations.support: tools/validate_lineage.py and the C007 genealogy enforce derived_from and delta_from_parents.
